anti_overlap: Source independence, corroboration counting, and whether 952 rows at 2+ sources is a defensible evidentiary population — owned by the transmission-criticism reviewer.
Correlation estimation mechanics, measurement invariance, and factor structure as statistical craft — owned by the psychometrics reviewer; this lens treats estimates only as loaded sections.
Property-graph modeling, reification patterns, and schema or loader syntax — owned by the ontology reviewer; this lens owns forces, sequence, and joints, not type systems.
Archetype theory, sign/object/interpretant analysis, and motif-index classification — owned by the semiotics reviewer.
Reference-frame roles (destination, bearing, reference, mark) and coordinate-free reckoning — owned by the wayfinding reviewer.
Copyright, paraphrase, glossing practice, and how an entry is worded — out of scope here.
decision_lens: Trace the load before judging the design: what work the symbol tier does, which member carries it, where the thrust exits. Then inspect the joint — a rigid tie between differently-founded works fails before either work does, so prefer a declared movement joint. Ask whether each member is structure or centering before asking if it is well made. Rank an option worse when it sets mortar that cannot be un-set than when it merely adds no capability. Name the unfounded buttress in every mitigation.
distance_rationale: The five lenses already on this question are all lenses on REPRESENTATION — how an entity is typed (ontology), how its numbers behave (psychometrics), what it means (semiotics), how it is reckoned against (etak), and how well it is attested (isnad). None of them is a lens on FORCE, SEQUENCE, or JOINTS. Pre-modern vaulting is a centuries-refined empirical discipline whose entire subject matter is what happens when you add mass to a standing structure: where the thrust goes, whether the section under it can carry, what the seam between new work and old does when both settle, what cannot be un-set once laid, and in what order courses may be raised. It shares no parent discipline with textual criticism, statistics, software architecture, mythology, or navigation, and it is not an AI-cliche domain. It owns four questions Options A–D never ask: (1) what LOAD does the symbol tier carry — which downstream consumer demands it — since a member sized without a stated span is unsized; (2) is the tier a permanent member or CENTERING, essential during construction and wrong to leave in place; (3) is the being/symbol seam BONDED or a continuous vertical joint that shears; and (4) since beings are founded at 29/29 and symbols at 5/29, is the shared universal-5 spine a rigid tie across differently-founded works, where the mason's remedy is a declared movement joint rather than a stronger tie. It also supplies the strongest unlisted option: the squinch. When two geometries will not meet, a mason does not deform either — he builds a third element belonging to neither, whose only job is transition.
expected_isomorphisms: Differential settlement between separately founded works ↔ beings founded at 29/29 coverage and symbols at 5/29 tied rigidly through one covariance gate and one stamped baseline: the tie tears before either work does, and the mason's remedy is not a stronger tie but a declared movement joint (separate schema, separate gate, separate baseline). Option A's 'shared spine for comparability' is exactly the rigid tie the vernacular forbids.

The middle-third rule and the thrust line ↔ it is not the 952 nodes, it is where the load lands. Symbol data can only enter the correlation population for the 10 pairs among the universal five (heat-ledger f-012); that is a narrow section carrying the whole added mass, while the relatedness V=801 universe is a different member entirely. Adding to one does not relieve the other, and 'the corpus is big enough to absorb it' is a volume argument where a section argument is required.

Centering / falsework struck at closure ↔ the unasked question of whether the symbol tier is a permanent member at all. Centering is essential, genuinely load-bearing while the ring is raised, and wrong to leave in place. A symbol layer that exists to derive archetypal signal into being vectors and then is struck (never shipping as node class, never entering V, never entering the gate) is a distinct option Options A–D cannot express, because all four assume the tier is permanent.

An arch carries nothing until it closes ↔ the '952 as pilot population' framing. A half-built ring is not half the value; it is zero structural value at full centering cost. If the archetypal register only pays off when a closed set of symbols is present (so that jawnsight and the 47-family clustering can actually read it), then a partial promotion is pure scaffolding expense, and the real question is the minimum closed ring, not the maximum defensible population.

The squinch / muqarnas transition zone ↔ the unlisted Option E: when a square room will not meet a round dome, you build a third element belonging to neither. Not a shared spine (A), not a separate axis set (C), but a small, purpose-built, independently-gated correspondence layer whose only job is converting between the being space and a symbol register — owned by neither collection, versioned on its own, and strikeable if the conversion stops holding.

Bond, toothing, and stack-bond shear ↔ two sub-corpora that overlap on five axes and nothing else. Contact is not bond; units must overlap ACROSS the joint for two masses to act as one. Five shared axes out of 29 with the other 24 not-applicable is a wall with a continuous vertical joint at the being/symbol seam — it looks tied and shears. The complementary move is raking back: build now in a way that deliberately leaves the bond open for a later course, rather than closing the schema against it.

Green mortar and lift height ↔ constraint 7 (entries with live citations are never replaced) and the covariance ratchet's stamped baseline. Both are mortar that cannot be un-set. Masons cap courses per day because green mortar squeezes under load and puts the wall permanently out of plumb; promoting 952 rows in a single lift before the symbol axis definitions have cured is the same error, and the ratchet will read the resulting drift as a fact about the corpus rather than as creep.

The buttress that must itself be founded ↔ every mitigation on the table (a symbol-specific schema, a second covariance gate, a second relatedness baseline, a new promotion criterion). Each is new mass added to resist a thrust, and each needs its own foundation — an owner, a gate, a stamped baseline of its own. An unfounded buttress is not a mitigation; it is the next thing to fail.

The voussoir versus the rubble core ↔ the census registry versus canon. A wall has facing units that carry and a fill that only occupies. Some of the 4,839 rows are fill — indexing material that should stay in the registry doing registry work — and the design's real question may be which symbols are voussoirs, not how to give all of them coordinates.
focus: Whether each option states the load the symbol tier must carry and traces it to ground; whether the being/symbol seam is bonded or a rigid tie across differently-founded works; whether the tier is a permanent member or centering to be struck; and what each option sets in mortar that cannot afterwards be un-set.
name: fd-masonry-thrust-and-settlement
persona: Apply the perspective of a master mason of pre-modern vaulting — Nubian and Persian brick domes raised without centering. It reads any addition as load: where it enters, what path it takes to ground, what the seam between new work and old does once both settle. It knows an arch carries nothing until it closes, that mortar cannot be un-set, that a wall shears at a joint that looked tight, that a buttress is mass which must itself be founded, and that two geometries refusing to meet need a third.
review_areas: Load path: name which consumer (covariance gate, 47-family clustering, relatedness V=801, jawnsight grammar) actually demands symbols. A member sized without a stated span is unsized — say so.
Middle-third test: it is not 952 nodes, it is where load lands. Show which estimate each option loads — the 10 pairs among the universal five, V, cluster drift — and whether it carries.
Differential settlement: beings at 29/29 and symbols at 5/29 are separately founded works. Is Option A's shared spine a rigid tie across that joint? Would a movement joint beat a stronger tie?
Bond, not contact: sub-corpora overlapping on five axes and nothing else form a continuous vertical joint. Test each option for real bond versus stack-bond shear at the being/symbol seam.
Centering or member: is the symbol tier structure, or falsework struck at closure — a derivation input that never ships as nodes? Propose the strikeable variant if no listed option holds it.
The squinch move: two geometries that will not meet need a third belonging to neither. Develop the transition-tier option — an independently-gated correspondence layer — enough to kill or keep.
Closure economics: an arch carries nothing until closed, so a 952-row pilot may be zero value at full centering cost. State the minimum closed ring and whether promotion criteria can produce one.
Green mortar: constraint 7 (citation-stable entries are never replaced) and the stamped covariance baseline cannot be un-set. Flag any option laying a full lift before symbol axis definitions cure.
Unfounded buttresses: each mitigation (symbol schema, second gate, second baseline, new promotion rule) is mass needing its own foundation — owner, gate, stamped baseline. Name the one lacking it.
Voussoir versus fill: ask which of the 4,839 registry rows actually carry and which are fill that stays in the registry, making the question which symbols bear load, not how to coordinate all.

severity_examples.condition: When any option admits symbol entries into `pnpm check:eidogen-covariance` or the relatedness build while also using shared axes as the being↔symbol comparability spine, with no separate gate, separate baseline, or declared movement joint.
severity_examples.scenario: New work is tied rigidly to old across differently-founded sections: symbols at 5/29 coverage share the universal-five spine with beings at 29/29 inside one covariance population and one stamped baseline. The tie is what fails, not either corpus — the ratchet reports drift in max |r|, redundant-pair census, and named-cluster membership with no way to distinguish settlement of the new work from a real change in the being corpus, and the baseline it compares against is itself the thing that moved.

severity_examples.condition: When a promotion of the symbol tier happens as a single population-wide event rather than as courses, with no stated cure step between lifts and no ability to revise a promoted entry's axis semantics.
severity_examples.scenario: The full lift is laid before the mortar cures: ~952 symbol rows are promoted in one pass under axis definitions that have never been exercised, and because citation-stable entries are never replaced, the definitions harden with the entries. When the symbol axes are later found to mean something different from the being axes of the same name, the corpus is permanently out of plumb and the only remedies are a schema weakening or a parallel un-citable collection.

severity_examples.condition: When an option's safety argument depends on a new gate, schema, or baseline that is named but given no owner, no stamped reference, and no CI entry point.
severity_examples.scenario: A mitigation is added as unfounded mass: a symbol-specific schema, a second covariance gate, or a second relatedness baseline is proposed to absorb the thrust, but nothing states who stamps it, what it ratchets against, or when it is checked. The buttress becomes the failure — it silently stops gating while the design continues to claim the risk is carried.

source_domain: Pre-modern load-bearing masonry and vault construction — Nubian and Persian/Central Asian brick vaults raised in inclined courses without centering, the squinch and muqarnas transition zone that joins a square room to a round dome, and the mason's empirical statics: the funicular thrust line and the middle-third rule, centering as temporary structure struck only at closure, bond and toothing across a joint, lift height and green-mortar creep, differential settlement between separately founded works, the deliberate movement joint that refuses to tie new work rigidly to old, and buttressing as dead load that must itself be founded.
success_hints: Lead with the span, not the member: an option that cannot name which consumer it serves is unsized, and saying so is worth more than any critique of its axis list.
Prefer a joint argument to a volume argument — differential settlement between 5/29 and 29/29 works bites harder and is more actionable than the 952-node count.
Develop the squinch (transition-tier) option far enough to be killed or kept: what it stores, which gate owns it, what happens when the conversion stops holding.
Ask of every option what cannot be un-set once built, and put that irreversibility in the finding itself rather than in a trailing caveat.
When an option survives, state its lift plan: how many courses, cured how, checked against what, before the next course is laid.
task_context: Determine how the jawnomicon symbol tier should be structured: what vector (if any) a symbol entry carries, how symbols relate to the existing 29-axis eidogen space for beings, and where symbols sit in the graph and relatedness layers. Surface options beyond the four already listed, especially any that question whether a symbol should be a node with coordinates at all. Attack each option against the measured constraints: the five universal axes, the covariance ratchet's pairwise-deletion estimates, the hygiene-09 V-shrinkage lesson, the strict 29-key creature schema, and the downstream jawnsight grammar. Target document: docs/symbol-tier-design-question.md (jawnomicon-nhe.3).
